clue.text: Unexpected things the author had found in graves?

indicators.note: the author's words are found inside the other piece, so one sits within the other

parts.note: grave accents are marks over letters, so graves are accents
the author is the setter, I; 'I had' contracts to I'D

explanation.surface: A writer discovers odd objects while poking around in graves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graves' looks like burial places but is the accent mark over a letter, as in French; 'found in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidents are events that happen by chance, without being planned or expected.

clue.text: What is at the heart of modern cycling?

indicators.note: letters cycle round, so the front pair of the word for modern rides round to the back

parts.note: something modern is recent

explanation.surface: A question about what really matters in today's cycling culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves RE from the front of RECENT to its end. With 9 Across the answer also signposts the CENTRE REGION of the grid, where the theme sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of anything is its core, the part at its middle.

clue.text: Win race by one second in 2 9?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letters of one and second sit next to the rest

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to land something is to win it, as in landing a contract
a race of people is a nation

explanation.surface: Someone wins a race by a single second, apparently somewhere central.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 9 is CENTRE REGION: the theme is Kiribati, the island nation sitting where all four hemispheres meet, and its islands TARAWA and BANABA appear in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiribati, the theme, is a country made of islands lying at the centre of the globe's hemispheres.

clue.text: Vessel whose cargo is targeted by soldiers?

definitions.text: Vessel whose cargo is targeted by soldiers?

parts.words: Vessel whose cargo is targeted by soldiers?
parts.note: soldiers are thin strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg; the vessel is the small cup holding that egg

explanation.surface: A ship whose freight is the target of a military attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers, in Britain, are fingers of toast for dipping into a boiled egg; 'Vessel' is a small holder, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holds the boiled egg at breakfast while toast soldiers are dipped into its yolk.

clue.text: Shock effect of dishevelled man wearing crumpled suit

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one set of letters goes within the other
a crumpled suit is messed up, so these letters are disordered
a dishevelled man is untidy, so his letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A scruffy man in a creased suit makes a startling impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'crumpled' and 'dishevelled' are anagram signals, one for each word; 'wearing' then puts the scrambled man inside the scrambled suit (TSUI).
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea wave is the aftermath of an undersea earthquake, the shock's effect.

clue.text: Divorced father assessed following case of self-abuse

indicators.note: the father and assessed pieces come after the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, so its first and last letters

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father
something assessed has been rated

explanation.surface: A divorced father has been judged after a case of self-harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who have divorced have parted, living apart from each other.

clue.text: New kind of TV is making plot-based feature?

parts.note: digital television replaced analogue broadcasts

explanation.surface: A modern television format is creating a film with a strong storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot-based feature' suggests a film, but the plot is a garden plot: digitalis is the foxglove.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove is a common garden plant, a feature growing in a flower bed or plot.

clue.text: I saw accommodating woman in order to be overwhelmed

indicators.note: to accommodate someone is to house them, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them, so saw means dated
a nun is a woman in a religious order

explanation.surface: I watched a helpful woman, all in order to be swamped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' signals the container; 'in order' belongs with 'woman' (a religious order), not with 'to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated literally means flooded, and figuratively swamped with more than one can handle.

clue.text: Area 51's not part of belief system

indicators.note: being not part of the word means these letters are taken out of it

parts.note: a religion is a system of belief
51 in Roman numerals is LI

explanation.surface: Area 51, the secret US base, is no part of any faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area 51' reads as the famous US military site, but 'Area' is the definition and 51 is LI. With 2 Down it signposts the CENTRE REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is a district or expanse, a synonym of area.

clue.text: Having some correspondence with figure representing North America in Australia

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in Australia, so they sit inside its letters

parts.note: a logo is a figure or emblem representing a company

explanation.surface: A symbol for North America found Down Under partly resembles something.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous things are comparable, similar in some respects without being identical.

clue.text: See 3
Primate published article about diversity mainly

indicators.note: the published piece goes about the other, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a book that is out has been published

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a range is a variety, so diversity
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news item on diversity about an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the final letter; 'about' signals the container round the trimmed word.
explanation.definitionFit: The orangutan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, so a primate.

clue.text: 3 sound sheepish about arrest

indicators.note: the sheep's noise goes about the other word, surrounding it

parts.note: a sheep's sound is baa
to nab someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Bleating sheepishly when being collared.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is ISLAND, the first word of 3 Down; Banaba is one of the islands of Kiribati, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Banaba is a raised coral island in the Pacific belonging to Kiribati.

clue.text: Sectarian party last to cast stigma off

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are rearranged
last to means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A party, the last to throw off a stigma, is sectarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges STIGMA to GMATIS; 'last to cast' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sectarian clings rigidly to the doctrines of a sect, much as a dogmatist insists on fixed beliefs.

clue.text: Student leaves stupid call smiling inanely

indicators.note: the student leaves the word, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: simple can mean stupid
L is a learner, a student driver's plate
to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A pupil exits after a foolish phone call, grinning stupidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpering means smiling in an affected, silly way, an idiot's grin.

clue.text: Documents reporter's income for each piece

indicators.note: what a reporter says is spoken, so the words are as heard

parts.note: pay per work: wages paid for each piece of work

explanation.surface: A journalist's earnings per article are documented.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'pay per work' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperwork is the forms and records that make up official documents.

clue.text: Drink and go round naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: to skirt something is to go round it

explanation.surface: Have a drink and wander about with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur.

clue.text: School abandons vulgar uniform

indicators.note: the school abandons the word, so its letters are dropped

parts.note: kitsch is vulgar, tasteless art or design

explanation.surface: A school drops its tasteless uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A kit is the set of clothing worn by a team, its uniform.

clue.text: Make fun of progressive characters in right-on liberal bubble

indicators.note: progressive means advancing step by step, so the letter taken moves on one place per word, starting with the first
characters are letters; the progression reaches the second letter of the middle word
in the last word, the progression has reached its third letter

explanation.surface: Mocking the woke, left-leaning echo chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progressive characters' takes letter 1 of 'right-on', letter 2 of 'liberal' and letter 3 of 'bubble'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to tease them good-naturedly.

clue.text: Japan's 16 miles east of old capital and close to Shanghai

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so miles follows

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A Japanese document routed through a far eastern capital, near Shanghai.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is PAPERWORK: origami is the Japanese art of folding paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is paper craft from Japan, literally a piece of work made of paper.

clue.text: Couple is last in prize list

parts.note: a couple are an item

indicators.note: the last in the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A pair comes last in a competition, then gets ranked.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, so to list.

clue.text: Shot decapitated Buffalo Bill?

indicators.note: decapitated means the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a shot at something is a stab

explanation.surface: A shot that beheaded the Wild West showman.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffalo Bill is the showman, but here it is a bill in Buffalo, a US city: Americans call a bill a tab.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a tab is the bill for drinks or a meal.

clue.text: What could be primarily available via on-line shop?

definitions.text: What could be primarily available via on-line shop?

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the first letters of each word

parts.note: Ocado is a British online grocery retailer

explanation.surface: Asking what you could buy, mainly, from an internet grocer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ocado is a British online supermarket; the whole clue describes the answer, a fruit it sells.
explanation.definitionFit: An online grocer sells fruit, and an avocado is one such item that could be bought there.

clue.text: Fool complied with guards leading priest

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: met as in met demands, complied with them
a team that is up is leading

explanation.surface: An idiot obeyed the guards escorting the cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Muppet is British slang for an idiot, from the puppet characters.

clue.text: Previous head of state oppressed by class

indicators.note: in a down answer, being pressed under the class word puts this piece below it

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British head of state

explanation.surface: An earlier leader crushed by the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the ruling class; 'class' is a school form.
explanation.definitionFit: Former describes something that came before, earlier in time.

clue.text: 50% of capital invested in modest settlement

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: coy means modest or shy

indicators.note: half of the word, its first three letters

explanation.surface: Half the city's money put into a humble housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is London, and half of it is LON.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a settlement founded in another land by incomers.

clue.text: Revolutionary Polish artist's upset fund manager

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to polish is to rub

indicators.note: in a down answer upset means turned upside down, so read in reverse

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist, plus the S

explanation.surface: A rebellious Polish painter troubles a finance boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursar manages the finances of a school or college.

clue.text: Pout about refusal to record one's speech

indicators.note: the pout goes about the other pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: a moue is a pout
no is a refusal
to log is to record

explanation.surface: Sulking over being refused permission to tape a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A monologue is a long speech by a single performer.

clue.text: Tearaway blowing limits of everybody's capital

indicators.note: blowing means losing, as in blowing a chance, so these letters go
limits are the outer edges, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A wild youngster who blows everyone's money in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarawa is the capital of Kiribati, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarawa is an atoll that is the seat of government of Kiribati.

clue.text: Rebuild her famous home for Tiller Girls?

indicators.note: to rebuild is to put together anew, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Refurbishing the celebrated residence of a dance troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tiller Girls were a famous British dance troupe; here tillers are girls who till the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls working the soil would live on a farm, so this rural dwelling is their home.

clue.text: Firm taking on new railway guard

indicators.note: taking on means admitting, so the new piece goes inside the firm word

parts.note: firm, as of jelly, means set

explanation.surface: A company hires a fresh railway guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' suggests a company but means set, and 'guard' looks like the railway job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier keeping watch, a guard.

clue.text: Pay attention to vehicle reversing in confined space

parts.note: to court someone is to pay attention to them

indicators.note: a reversing vehicle goes backwards, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: a dray is a cart

explanation.surface: Watch out for a truck backing up in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard is an open area enclosed by walls or buildings.
